page: OVHcloud a10-180 is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9554 processor with 120 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 170.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.42 GB per core. Graphics processing is driven by four NVIDIA Ampere A10 GPUs, providing a combined total of 96 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 400 GB SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations place this server in the top tier for multi-core processing and specialized workloads. The multi-core stress-ng CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores both rank in the top 10%, supported by strong single-core performance. The system demonstrates high throughput in cryptographic and vector calculations, as evidenced by top-tier results in Passmark encryption and extended instructions tests. In LLM inference benchmarks, the server achieves top-tier performance across small, medium, and large models, processing 330.75 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 70B model.

While the server delivers high compute density with 120 dedicated physical cores and substantial GPU resources, the memory-to-core ratio is relatively low at 1.42 GB per core, which may limit memory-intensive applications that do not offload to GPU VRAM. The local storage capacity is also constrained to 400 GB SSD, requiring external storage solutions for large datasets. Qualitatively, the server offers high resource density for parallel computing and machine learning workloads, balancing high-end GPU acceleration with a dense multi-core CPU configuration.
This hardware profile is suited for machine learning inference, large language model execution, parallel data processing, software compilation, and graphics-intensive tasks such as ray tracing.
